name_translation: The Yoga of Liberation through Renunciation

verses.speaker: अर्जुन उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
संन्यासस्य महाबाहो तत्त्वमिच्छामि वेदितुम् |
त्यागस्य च हृषीकेश पृथक्केशिनिषूदन || १ ||
verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
संन्यासस्य महाबाहो तत्त्वमिच्छामि वेदितुम् |
त्यागस्य च हृषीकेश पृथक्केशिनिषूदन || १ ||
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca |
sannyāsasya mahābāho tattvamicchāmi veditum |
tyāgasya ca hṛṣīkeśa pṛthakkeśiniṣūdana || 1 ||
verses.word_meanings: arjunaḥ uvāca—Arjuna said; sannyāsasya—of renunciation (Sannyasa); mahā-bāho—O mighty-armed one; tattvam—the essential truth; icchāmi—I desire; veditum—to understand; tyāgasya—of relinquishment (Tyaga); ca—and; hṛṣīkeśa—O Master of the senses; pṛthak—distinctly / separately; keśi-niṣūdana—O slayer of the Keshi demon.
verses.translation: Arjuna said: O mighty-armed Krishna, O Hrishikesha, O slayer of the Keshi demon! I desire to understand distinctly the true essence of renunciation (Sannyāsa) and of relinquishment (Tyāga).
verses.meaning: Arjuna opens the climactic chapter of the Gita with a definitive request for clarity on two key spiritual terms that have recurred throughout the dialogue: Sannyasa (external renunciation of actions) and Tyaga (internal relinquishment of the fruits of action).
verses.purport: Arjuna opens the climactic chapter of the Gita with a definitive request for clarity on two key spiritual terms that have recurred throughout the dialogue: Sannyasa (external renunciation of actions) and Tyaga (internal relinquishment of the fruits of action).

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
काम्यानां कर्मणां न्यासं संन्यासं कवयो विदुः |
सर्वकर्मफलत्यागं प्राहुस्त्यागं विचक्षणाः || २ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
काम्यानां कर्मणां न्यासं संन्यासं कवयो विदुः |
सर्वकर्मफलत्यागं प्राहुस्त्यागं विचक्षणाः || २ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
kāmyānāṃ karmaṇāṃ nyāsaṃ sannyāsaṃ kavayo viduḥ |
sarvakarmaphalatyāgaṃ prāhustyāgaṃ vicakṣaṇāḥ || 2 ||
verses.word_meanings: śrī-bhagavān uvāca—the Supreme Lord said; kāmyānām karmaṇām—of actions prompted by selfish desire; nyāsam—renunciation/abandonment; sannyāsam—Sannyasa; kavayaḥ—the learned sages; viduḥ—know/declare; sarva-karma-phala-tyāgam—renunciation of the fruits of all actions; prāhuḥ—declare; tyāgam—Tyaga; vicakṣaṇāḥ—the discerning wise.
verses.translation: The Supreme Lord said: The learned sages declare that renunciation of desire-prompted actions (Kamya Karma) is Sannyāsa; the discerning wise declare that relinquishing the fruits of all actions is Tyāga.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna defines the core difference: Sannyasa is discarding desire-driven projects, while Tyaga is relinquishing possessiveness and expectation of rewards while executing all righteous duties.
verses.purport: Sri Krishna defines the core difference: Sannyasa is discarding desire-driven projects, while Tyaga is relinquishing possessiveness and expectation of rewards while executing all righteous duties.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
त्याज्यं दोषवदित्येके कर्म प्राहुर्मनीषिणः |
यज्ञदानतपःकर्म न त्याज्यमिति चापरे || ३ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
त्याज्यं दोषवदित्येके कर्म प्राहुर्मनीषिणः |
यज्ञदानतपःकर्म न त्याज्यमिति चापरे || ३ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
tyājyaṃ doṣavadityeke karma prāhurmanīṣiṇaḥ |
yajñadānatapaḥkarma na tyājyamiti cāpare || 3 ||
verses.word_meanings: tyājyam—must be given up; doṣa-vat—as an evil/fault; iti—thus; eke—some; karma—action; prāhuḥ—say; manīṣiṇaḥ—thinkers/philosophers; yajña-dāna-tapaḥ-karma—acts of sacrifice, charity, and austerity; na tyājyam—should never be given up; iti ca apare—thus say others.
verses.translation: Some philosophers declare that all action should be abandoned as full of fault, while other sages declare that acts of sacrifice, charity, and austerity should never be abandoned.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna summarizes the historical debate between radical asceticism (which claimed all karma causes bondage) and the Mimamsaka/Vedic view of preserving sacred duties.
verses.purport: Sri Krishna summarizes the historical debate between radical asceticism (which claimed all karma causes bondage) and the Mimamsaka/Vedic view of preserving sacred duties.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
निश्चयं शृणु मे तत्र त्यागे भरतसत्तम |
त्यागो हि पुरुषव्याघ्र त्रिविधः सम्प्रकीर्तितः || ४ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
निश्चयं शृणु मे तत्र त्यागे भरतसत्तम |
त्यागो हि पुरुषव्याघ्र त्रिविधः सम्प्रकीर्तितः || ४ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
niścayaṃ śṛṇu me tatra tyāge bharatasattama |
tyāgo hi puruṣavyāghra trividhaḥ samprakīrtitaḥ || 4 ||
verses.word_meanings: niścayam—definitive conclusion; śṛṇu—hear; me—from Me; tatra—in this matter; tyāge—regarding renunciation (Tyaga); bharata-sat-tama—O best of the Bharatas; tyāgaḥ hi—for relinquishment; puruṣa-vyāghra—O tiger among men; tri-vidhaḥ—threefold; samprakīrtitaḥ—is declared.
verses.translation: Hear now My definitive conclusion on this matter of relinquishment, O best of the Bharatas. Relinquishment (Tyāga), O tiger among men, is declared to be of three kinds.
verses.meaning: The Lord prepares to deliver His conclusive verdict on the threefold categorization of renunciation across the modes of Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas.
verses.purport: The Lord prepares to deliver His conclusive verdict on the threefold categorization of renunciation across the modes of Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यज्ञदानतपःकर्म न त्याज्यं कार्यमेव तत् |
यज्ञो दानं तपश्चैव पावनानि मनीषिणाम् || ५ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यज्ञदानतपःकर्म न त्याज्यं कार्यमेव तत् |
यज्ञो दानं तपश्चैव पावनानि मनीषिणाम् || ५ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
yajñadānatapaḥkarma na tyājyaṃ kāryameva tat |
yajño dānaṃ tapaścaiva pāvanāni manīṣiṇām || 5 ||
verses.word_meanings: yajña-dāna-tapaḥ-karma—acts of sacrifice, charity, and austerity; na tyājyam—must not be relinquished; kāryam eva tat—they must certainly be performed; yajñaḥ—sacrifice; dānam—charity; tapaḥ ca eva—and austerity indeed; pāvanāni—purifiers; manīṣiṇām—of the wise.
verses.translation: Acts of sacrifice (Yajña), charity (Dāna), and austerity (Tapas) should never be abandoned; they must indeed be performed. For sacrifice, charity, and austerity are the purifiers of the wise.
verses.meaning: Sacred actions purify the intellect and burn away latent egoism. They should never be discarded by any spiritual seeker.
verses.purport: Sacred actions purify the intellect and burn away latent egoism. They should never be discarded by any spiritual seeker.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
एतान्यपि तु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा फलानि च |
कर्तव्यानीति मे पार्थ निश्चितं मतमुत्तमम् || ६ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
एतान्यपि तु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा फलानि च |
कर्तव्यानीति मे पार्थ निश्चितं मतमुत्तमम् || ६ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
etānyapi tu karmāṇi saṅgaṃ tyaktvā phalāni ca |
kartavyānīti me pārtha niścitaṃ matamuttamam || 6 ||
verses.word_meanings: etāni api tu karmāṇi—even these actions; saṅgam—attachment/possessiveness; tyaktvā—renouncing; phalāni ca—and the desire for fruits; kartavyāni iti—must be performed as duty; me—My; pārtha—O Partha; niścitam—definite; matam uttamam—supreme verdict.
verses.translation: Even these sacred actions must be performed renouncing attachment and all desire for fruits. This, O Partha, is My firm and supreme verdict.
verses.meaning: This is Sri Krishna's definitive stance: Action itself is not the problem; attachment (*Sanga*) and craving for fruits (*Phala-kanksha*) are the sole roots of bondage.
verses.purport: This is Sri Krishna's definitive stance: Action itself is not the problem; attachment (*Sanga*) and craving for fruits (*Phala-kanksha*) are the sole roots of bondage.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
नियतस्य तु संन्यासः कर्मणो नोपपद्यते |
मोहात्तस्य परित्यागस्तामसः परिकीर्तितः || ७ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
नियतस्य तु संन्यासः कर्मणो नोपपद्यते |
मोहात्तस्य परित्यागस्तामसः परिकीर्तितः || ७ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
niyatasya tu sannyāsaḥ karmaṇo nopapadyate |
mohāttasya parityāgastāmasaḥ parikīrtitaḥ || 7 ||
verses.word_meanings: niyatasya tu—of prescribed/obligatory; sannyāsaḥ karmaṇaḥ—renunciation of duty; na upapadyate—is never justifiable/proper; mohāt—out of delusion/ignorance; tasya—its; parityāgaḥ—abandonment; tāmasaḥ—Tamasic; parikīrtitaḥ—is declared.
verses.translation: Renunciation of prescribed obligatory duty is never proper. Abandoning one's duty out of delusion and ignorance is declared to be Tamasic.
verses.meaning: Giving up duties because of laziness, apathy, or confusion is Tamasic escapism, not spiritual renunciation.
verses.purport: Giving up duties because of laziness, apathy, or confusion is Tamasic escapism, not spiritual renunciation.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
दुःखमित्येव यत्कर्म कायक्लेशभयात्त्यजेत् |
स कृत्वा राजसं त्यागं नैव त्यागफलं लभेत् || ८ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
दुःखमित्येव यत्कर्म कायक्लेशभयात्त्यजेत् |
स कृत्वा राजसं त्यागं नैव त्यागफलं लभेत् || ८ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
duḥkhamityeva yatkarma kāyakleśabhayāttyajet |
sa kṛtvā rājasaṃ tyāgaṃ naiva tyāgaphalaṃ labhet || 8 ||
verses.word_meanings: duḥkham iti eva—simply because it is troublesome/painful; yat karma—whatever duty; kāya-kleśa-bhayāt—out of fear of physical strain/discomfort; tyajet—abandons; saḥ—he; kṛtvā—having performed; rājasam tyāgam—Rajasic renunciation; na eva—certainly not; tyāga-phalam—the fruit of true renunciation; labhet—obtains.
verses.translation: Whoever abandons obligatory duty simply because it is difficult or out of fear of physical discomfort performs Rajasic renunciation; such a person certainly does not attain the spiritual fruit of true renunciation.
verses.meaning: Avoiding hard work or social obligations because they are strenuous is Rajasic avoidance, which brings no spiritual elevation.
verses.purport: Avoiding hard work or social obligations because they are strenuous is Rajasic avoidance, which brings no spiritual elevation.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
कार्यमित्येव यत्कर्म नियतं क्रियतेऽर्जुन |
सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा फलं चैव स त्यागः सात्त्विको मतः || ९ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
कार्यमित्येव यत्कर्म नियतं क्रियतेऽर्जुन |
सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा फलं चैव स त्यागः सात्त्विको मतः || ९ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
kāryamityeva yatkarma niyataṃ kriyate'rjuna |
saṅgaṃ tyaktvā phalaṃ caiva sa tyāgaḥ sāttviko mataḥ || 9 ||
verses.word_meanings: kāryam iti eva—as an obligatory duty that must be done; yat karma niyatam—whatever prescribed action; kriyate—is performed; arjuna—O Arjuna; saṅgam tyaktvā—relinquishing attachment; phalam ca eva—and the fruit indeed; saḥ tyāgaḥ—that relinquishment; sāttvikaḥ mataḥ—is regarded as Sattvic.
verses.translation: When obligatory duty is performed simply because it ought to be done, relinquishing attachment and all desire for fruits, O Arjuna, that relinquishment is regarded as Sattvic.
verses.meaning: Sattvic Tyaga is the golden path of Karma Yoga: Doing one's work with dedication as a divine offering without seeking personal reward or identifying with egotistical ownership.
verses.purport: Sattvic Tyaga is the golden path of Karma Yoga: Doing one's work with dedication as a divine offering without seeking personal reward or identifying with egotistical ownership.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
न द्वेष्ट्यकुशलं कर्म कुशले नानुषज्जते |
त्यागी सत्त्वसमाविष्टो मेधावी छिन्नसंशयः || १० ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
न द्वेष्ट्यकुशलं कर्म कुशले नानुषज्जते |
त्यागी सत्त्वसमाविष्टो मेधावी छिन्नसंशयः || १० ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
na dveṣṭyakuśalaṃ karma kuśale nānuṣajjate |
tyāgī sattvasamāviṣṭo medhāvī chinnasaṃśayaḥ || 10 ||
verses.word_meanings: na dveṣṭi—does not hate; akuśalam karma—unpleasant or disagreeable work; kuśale—in pleasant work; na anuṣajjate—does not become attached; tyāgī—the true renunciant; sattva-samāviṣṭaḥ—imbued with the quality of goodness (Sattva); medhāvī—endowed with spiritual wisdom; chinna-saṃśayaḥ—with all doubts cleaved asunder.
verses.translation: The wise renunciant imbued with Sattva, endowed with clear intellect and free from all doubts, neither hates disagreeable work nor clings with attachment to pleasant work.
verses.meaning: A Sattvic karma yogi maintains equanimity across all duties, performing whatever situation demands without resentment or personal bias.
verses.purport: A Sattvic karma yogi maintains equanimity across all duties, performing whatever situation demands without resentment or personal bias.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
न हि देहभृता शक्यं त्यक्तुं कर्माण्यशेषतः |
यस्तु कर्मफलत्यागी स त्यागीत्यभिधीयते || ११ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
न हि देहभृता शक्यं त्यक्तुं कर्माण्यशेषतः |
यस्तु कर्मफलत्यागी स त्यागीत्यभिधीयते || ११ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
na hi dehabhṛtā śakyaṃ tyaktuṃ karmāṇyaśeṣataḥ |
yastu karmaphalatyāgī sa tyāgītyabhidhīyate || 11 ||
verses.word_meanings: na hi—certainly not; deha-bhṛtā—by an embodied soul; śakyam—is possible; tyaktum—to renounce; karmāṇi—actions; aśeṣataḥ—completely/entirely; yaḥ tu—whoever however; karma-phala-tyāgī—relinquisher of the fruits of action; saḥ—he; tyāgī iti—as a true renunciant; abhidhīyate—is designated.
verses.translation: It is indeed impossible for an embodied being to renounce all actions entirely. But whoever renounces the fruits of action is truly called a renunciant (Tyāgī).
verses.meaning: As long as one has a physical body, biological and mental activities are inevitable. Therefore, true renunciation consists of relinquishing desire and ego, not physical cessation.
verses.purport: As long as one has a physical body, biological and mental activities are inevitable. Therefore, true renunciation consists of relinquishing desire and ego, not physical cessation.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अनिष्टमिष्टं मिश्रं च त्रिविधं कर्मणः फलम् |
भवत्यत्यागिनां प्रेत्य न तु संन्यासिनां क्वचित् || १२ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अनिष्टमिष्टं मिश्रं च त्रिविधं कर्मणः फलम् |
भवत्यत्यागिनां प्रेत्य न तु संन्यासिनां क्वचित् || १२ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
aniṣṭamiṣṭaṃ miśraṃ ca trividhaṃ karmaṇaḥ phalam |
bhavatyatyāgināṃ pretya na tu sannyāsināṃ kvacit || 12 ||
verses.word_meanings: aniṣṭam—unpleasant (hellish/suffering); iṣṭam—pleasant (heavenly/joyful); miśram ca—and mixed (human experience); tri-vidham—threefold; karmaṇaḥ phalam—fruit of action; bhavati—accrues; atyāginām—to non-renouncers (the attached); pretya—after death / in future; na tu—but not; sannyāsinām—to true renunciants; kvacit—at any time.
verses.translation: The threefold fruit of action—unpleasant, pleasant, and mixed—accrues after death to those who have not renounced; but never to the true renunciants (who have surrendered all fruits).
verses.meaning: Those attached to outcomes are bound to the wheel of samsara, experiencing pleasant, painful, or mixed karmic fruits. True renunciants transcend all karma.
verses.purport: Those attached to outcomes are bound to the wheel of samsara, experiencing pleasant, painful, or mixed karmic fruits. True renunciants transcend all karma.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
पञ्चैतानि महाबाहो कारणानि निबोध मे |
साङ्ख्ये कृतान्ते प्रोक्तानि सिद्धये सर्वकर्मणाम् || १३ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
पञ्चैतानि महाबाहो कारणानि निबोध मे |
साङ्ख्ये कृतान्ते प्रोक्तानि सिद्धये सर्वकर्मणाम् || १३ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
pañcaitāni mahābāho kāraṇāni nibodha me |
sāṅkhye kṛtānte proktāni siddhaye sarvakarmaṇām || 13 ||
verses.word_meanings: pañca etāni—these five; mahā-bāho—O mighty-armed one; kāraṇāni—causes/factors; nibodha—learn/understand; me—from Me; sāṅkhye kṛtānte—in the Samkhya/Vedanta doctrine of ultimate conclusion; proktāni—declared; siddhaye—for the accomplishment; sarva-karmaṇām—of all actions.
verses.translation: Learn from Me, O mighty-armed one, these five factors declared in the philosophical conclusion (Vedānta) for the accomplishment of all actions.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna introduces the profound metaphysical analysis of the five causes behind every human action, dismantling the illusion of individual ego-doership.
verses.purport: Sri Krishna introduces the profound metaphysical analysis of the five causes behind every human action, dismantling the illusion of individual ego-doership.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अधिष्ठानं तथा कर्ता करणं च पृथग्विधम् |
विविधाश्च पृथक्चेष्टा दैवं चैवात्र पञ्चमम् || १४ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अधिष्ठानं तथा कर्ता करणं च पृथग्विधम् |
विविधाश्च पृथक्चेष्टा दैवं चैवात्र पञ्चमम् || १४ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
adhiṣṭhānaṃ tathā kartā karaṇaṃ ca pṛthagvidham |
vividhāśca pṛthakceṣṭā daivaṃ caivātra pañcamam || 14 ||
verses.word_meanings: adhiṣṭhānam—the seat/substratum (the physical body); tathā—and; kartā—the doer (the empirical ego / Jiva); karaṇam ca—and the instruments (the senses and mind); pṛthak-vidham—of various kinds; vividhāḥ ca—and diverse; pṛthak ceṣṭāḥ—distinct vital efforts and activities (Pranas); daivam ca eva—and the divine/destiny / cosmic presiding deities; atra—here; pañcamam—the fifth factor.
verses.translation: The physical body (Adhiṣṭhāna), the ego-agent (Kartā), the various sensory instruments (Karaṇa), the diverse multiple endeavors (Ceṣṭā), and divine providence/cosmic will (Daiva) as the fifth factor.
verses.meaning: No action is performed by the soul alone. Every deed is a composite outcome of the physical vehicle, ego-identification, sensory tools, biological energies, and cosmic forces (Daiva).
verses.purport: No action is performed by the soul alone. Every deed is a composite outcome of the physical vehicle, ego-identification, sensory tools, biological energies, and cosmic forces (Daiva).

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
शरीरवाङ्मनोभिर्यत्कर्म प्रारभते नरः |
न्याय्यं वा विपरीतं वा पञ्चैते तस्य हेतवः || १५ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
शरीरवाङ्मनोभिर्यत्कर्म प्रारभते नरः |
न्याय्यं वा विपरीतं वा पञ्चैते तस्य हेतवः || १५ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
śarīravāṅmanobhiryatkarma prārabhate naraḥ |
nyāyyaṃ vā viparītaṃ vā pañcaite tasya hetavaḥ || 15 ||
verses.word_meanings: śarīra-vāṅ-manobhiḥ—with body, speech, and mind; yat karma—whatever action; prārabhate—undertakes/initiates; naraḥ—a human being; nyāyyam vā—whether righteous/lawful; viparītam vā—or contrary/unlawful; pañca ete—these five; tasya—of that; hetavaḥ—are the causes.
verses.translation: Whatever action a person undertakes by body, speech, or mind, whether it be righteous or unrighteous, these five are its causes.
verses.meaning: Every physical, verbal, and mental operation across all of human experience operates strictly through these five contributing factors.
verses.purport: Every physical, verbal, and mental operation across all of human experience operates strictly through these five contributing factors.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
तत्रैवं सति कर्तारमात्मानं केवलं तु यः |
पश्यत्यकृतबुद्धित्वान्न स पश्यति दुर्मतिः || १६ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
तत्रैवं सति कर्तारमात्मानं केवलं तु यः |
पश्यत्यकृतबुद्धित्वान्न स पश्यति दुर्मतिः || १६ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
tatraivaṃ sati kartāramātmānaṃ kevalaṃ tu yaḥ |
paśyatyakṛtabuddhittvānna sa paśyati durmatiḥ || 16 ||
verses.word_meanings: tatra evam sati—such being the case; kartāram—as the doer; ātmānam kevalam—the pure Self alone; tu yaḥ—whoever however; paśyati—views/sees; akṛta-buddhitvāt—due to unpurified intellect; na saḥ paśyati—he does not see truly; durmatiḥ—of distorted understanding.
verses.translation: Such being the case, whoever looks upon the pure Self alone as the doer, due to an unrefined intellect, is of perverted intelligence and does not see the truth.
verses.meaning: The pure Atman is the transcendent witness (Sakshi), unaffected by Prakriti's operations. Believing 'I am the doer' is the primal cognitive error.
verses.purport: The pure Atman is the transcendent witness (Sakshi), unaffected by Prakriti's operations. Believing 'I am the doer' is the primal cognitive error.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यस्य नाहङ्कृतो भावो बुद्धिर्यस्य न लिप्यते |
हत्वापि स इमाँल्लोकान्न हन्ति न निबध्यते || १७ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यस्य नाहङ्कृतो भावो बुद्धिर्यस्य न लिप्यते |
हत्वापि स इमाँल्लोकान्न हन्ति न निबध्यते || १७ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
yasya nāhaṅkṛto bhāvo buddhiryasya na lipyate |
hatvāpi sa imām̐llokānna hanti na nibadhyate || 17 ||
verses.word_meanings: yasya—whose; na ahaṅkṛtaḥ bhāvaḥ—state of mind is free from egotism; buddhiḥ yasya—whose intellect; na lipyate—is not tainted/attached; hatvā api—even though slaying; saḥ—he; imān lokān—these worlds/beings; na hanti—does not slay; na nibadhyate—nor is he bound.
verses.translation: One whose consciousness is free from egotism ('I am the doer') and whose intellect is untainted—even if such a person slays these beings in righteous battle, they neither slay nor are they bound by karma.
verses.meaning: This profound paradoxical verse directly addresses Arjuna's warrior duty: When an enlightened soul acts strictly as an instrument of divine cosmic order without personal ego, no karmic bondage is generated.
verses.purport: This profound paradoxical verse directly addresses Arjuna's warrior duty: When an enlightened soul acts strictly as an instrument of divine cosmic order without personal ego, no karmic bondage is generated.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं परिज्ञाता त्रिविधा कर्मचोदना |
करणं कर्म कर्तेति त्रिविधः कर्मसङ्ग्रहः || १८ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं परिज्ञाता त्रिविधा कर्मचोदना |
करणं कर्म कर्तेति त्रिविधः कर्मसङ्ग्रहः || १८ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ parijñātā trividhā karmacodanā |
karaṇaṃ karma karteti trividhaḥ karmasaṅgrahaḥ || 18 ||
verses.word_meanings: jñānam—knowledge; jñeyam—the object of knowledge; parijñātā—the knower; tri-vidhā—threefold; karma-codanā—impulse to action; karaṇam—the instrument; karma—the action itself; kartā iti—and the doer; tri-vidhaḥ—threefold; karma-saṅgrahaḥ—the basis/constituents of action.
verses.translation: Knowledge (Jñāna), the object of knowledge (Jñeya), and the knower (Parijñātā)—these three constitute the impulse to action. The instrument (Karaṇa), the action (Karma), and the doer (Kartā)—these three constitute the constituent basis of action.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna maps the cognitive triad that initiates any deed (Knower, Knowledge, Known) and the operational triad that executes it (Doer, Instrument, Action).
verses.purport: Sri Krishna maps the cognitive triad that initiates any deed (Knower, Knowledge, Known) and the operational triad that executes it (Doer, Instrument, Action).

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
ज्ञानं कर्म च कर्ता च त्रिधैव गुणभेदतः |
प्रोच्यते गुणसङ्ख्याने यथावच्छृणु तान्यपि || १९ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
ज्ञानं कर्म च कर्ता च त्रिधैव गुणभेदतः |
प्रोच्यते गुणसङ्ख्याने यथावच्छृणु तान्यपि || १९ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
jñānaṃ karma ca kartā ca tridhaiva guṇabhedataḥ |
procyate guṇasaṅkhyāne yathāvacchṛṇu tānyapi || 19 ||
verses.word_meanings: jñānam—knowledge; karma ca—and action; kartā ca—and the doer; tridhā eva—in three ways indeed; guṇa-bhedataḥ—according to the distinction of the gunas; procyate—are declared; guṇa-saṅkhyāne—in the philosophy of Gunas (Samkhya); yathāvat—duly/accurately; śṛṇu—hear; tāni api—about them also.
verses.translation: Knowledge, action, and the doer are declared in the science of the Guṇas (Sāṅkhya) to be of three kinds according to the distinction of the Guṇas. Hear now duly of these as well.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna now classifies the triad of Knowledge, Action, and Doer across Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas.
verses.purport: Sri Krishna now classifies the triad of Knowledge, Action, and Doer across Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
सर्वभूतेषु येनैकं भावमव्ययमीक्षते |
अविभक्तं विभक्तेषु तज्ज्ञानं विद्धि सात्त्विकम् || २० ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
सर्वभूतेषु येनैकं भावमव्ययमीक्षते |
अविभक्तं विभक्तेषु तज्ज्ञानं विद्धि सात्त्विकम् || २० ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
sarvabhūteṣu yenaikaṃ bhāvamavyayamīkṣate |
avibhaktaṃ vibhakteṣu tajjñānaṃ viddhi sāttvikam || 20 ||
verses.word_meanings: sarva-bhūteṣu—in all living beings; yena—by which; ekam—one; bhāvam avyayam—imperishable divine reality; īkṣate—one beholds; avibhaktam—undivided; vibhakteṣu—among the divided/diverse; tat jñānam—that knowledge; viddhi—know; sāttvikam—to be Sattvic (in the mode of goodness).
verses.translation: That knowledge by which one beholds the one imperishable, undivided Reality in all diverse living beings—know that knowledge to be Sattvic.
verses.meaning: Sattvic knowledge is holistic spiritual non-duality: Recognizing the one divine consciousness (Brahman) animating all multifaceted forms in creation.
verses.purport: Sattvic knowledge is holistic spiritual non-duality: Recognizing the one divine consciousness (Brahman) animating all multifaceted forms in creation.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
पृथक्त्वेन तु यज्ज्ञानं नानाभावान्पृथग्विधान् |
वेत्ति सर्वेषु भूतेषु तज्ज्ञानं विद्धि राजसम् || २१ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
पृथक्त्वेन तु यज्ज्ञानं नानाभावान्पृथग्विधान् |
वेत्ति सर्वेषु भूतेषु तज्ज्ञानं विद्धि राजसम् || २१ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
pṛthaktvena tu yajjñānaṃ nānābhāvānpṛthagvidhān |
vetti sarveṣu bhūteṣu tajjñānaṃ viddhi rājasam || 21 ||
verses.word_meanings: pṛthaktvena—as distinct/separate; tu—but; yat jñānam—which knowledge; nānā-bhāvān—manifold different existences; pṛthak-vidhān—of diverse kinds; vetti—perceives; sarveṣu bhūteṣu—in all living entities; tat jñānam—that knowledge; viddhi—know; rājasam—to be Rajasic (in the mode of passion).
verses.translation: But that knowledge which perceives manifold diverse existences as entirely separate and distinct in all beings—know that knowledge to be Rajasic.
verses.meaning: Rajasic knowledge sees fragmented separation, viewing individuals and entities as mutually isolated, competitive, and disconnected.
verses.purport: Rajasic knowledge sees fragmented separation, viewing individuals and entities as mutually isolated, competitive, and disconnected.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यत्तत्कृत्स्नवदेकस्मिन्कार्ये सक्तमहैतुकम् |
अतत्त्वार्थवदल्पं च तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् || २२ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यत्तत्कृत्स्नवदेकस्मिन्कार्ये सक्तमहैतुकम् |
अतत्त्वार्थवदल्पं च तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् || २२ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
yattatkṛtsnavadekasmiṅkārye saktamahaitukam |
atattvārthavadalpaṃ ca tattāmasamudāhṛtam || 22 ||
verses.word_meanings: yat tu—that which however; kṛtsna-vat—as if it were the whole; ekasmin kārye—to one single trivial effect/object; saktam—fanatically attached; ahaitukam—without reason / irrational; a-tattva-artha-vat—devoid of real truth/essence; alpam ca—and narrow/trivial; tat—that; tāmasam—Tamasic; udāhṛtam—is declared.
verses.translation: And that knowledge which clings fanatically to one single trivial object as if it were the whole, irrational, devoid of real essence, and narrow—that is declared to be Tamasic.
verses.meaning: Tamasic knowledge is dogmatic, superstitious, and narrow-minded, mistaking a single dogma, idol, or material fragment for the entirety of truth.
verses.purport: Tamasic knowledge is dogmatic, superstitious, and narrow-minded, mistaking a single dogma, idol, or material fragment for the entirety of truth.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
नियतं सङ्गरहितमरागद्वेषतः कृतम् |
अफलप्रेप्सुना कर्म यत्तत्सात्त्विकमुच्यते || २३ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
नियतं सङ्गरहितमरागद्वेषतः कृतम् |
अफलप्रेप्सुना कर्म यत्तत्सात्त्विकमुच्यते || २३ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
niyataṃ saṅgarahitamarāgadveṣataḥ kṛtam |
aphaiaprepsunā karma yattatsāttvikamucyate || 23 ||
verses.word_meanings: niyatam—prescribed/obligatory; saṅga-rahitam—free from attachment; arāga-dveṣataḥ—without personal attraction or aversion; kṛtam—performed; aphala-prepsunā—by one not desiring fruits; karma—action; yat—which; tat—that; sāttvikam ucyate—is called Sattvic.
verses.translation: Action that is obligatory, performed without attachment, free from attraction or aversion, and done by one desiring no reward—that is called Sattvic.
verses.meaning: Sattvic action is performed with pure focus on duty, with no selfish agenda, hatred, or craving.
verses.purport: Sattvic action is performed with pure focus on duty, with no selfish agenda, hatred, or craving.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यत्तु कामेप्सुना कर्म साहङ्कारेण वा पुनः |
क्रियते बहुलायासं तद्राजसमुदाहृतम् || २४ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यत्तु कामेप्सुना कर्म साहङ्कारेण वा पुनः |
क्रियते बहुलायासं तद्राजसमुदाहृतम् || २४ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
yattu kāmepsunā karma sāhaṅkāreṇa vā punaḥ |
kriyate bahulāyāsaṃ tadrājasamudāhṛtam || 24 ||
verses.word_meanings: yat tu—that which however; kāma-īpsunā—by one craving gratification of desires; karma—action; sa-ahaṅkāreṇa—with proud ego; vā punaḥ—or again; kriyate—is performed; bahula-āyāsam—with excessive strain and agitation; tat—that; rājasam—Rajasic; udāhṛtam—is exemplified.
verses.translation: But that action which is performed with excessive strain by one seeking the gratification of desires, or impelled by egotism—that is declared to be Rajasic.
verses.meaning: Rajasic action is characterized by intense agitation, stress, arrogance, and obsessive thirst for personal rewards.
verses.purport: Rajasic action is characterized by intense agitation, stress, arrogance, and obsessive thirst for personal rewards.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अनुबन्धं क्षयं हिंसामनपेक्ष्य च पौरुषम् |
मोहादारभ्यते कर्म यत्तत्तामसमुच्यते || २५ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अनुबन्धं क्षयं हिंसामनपेक्ष्य च पौरुषम् |
मोहादारभ्यते कर्म यत्तत्तामसमुच्यते || २५ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
anubandhaṃ kṣayaṃ hiṃsāmanapekṣya ca pauruṣam |
mohādārabhyate karma yattattāmasamucyate || 25 ||
verses.word_meanings: anubandham—future consequences; kṣayam—loss/destruction of resources; hiṃsām—harm and violence to others; anapekṣya—heedless of; ca—and; pauruṣam—one's own capacity; mohāt—out of delusion/blindness; ārabhyate—is undertaken; karma—action; yat—which; tat—that; tāmasam ucyate—is called Tamasic.
verses.translation: That action which is undertaken out of delusion, heedless of future consequences, destruction of wealth, injury to others, and one's own capability—that is called Tamasic.
verses.meaning: Tamasic action is reckless, destructive, and blind, disregarding ethical fallout and causing ruin to oneself and society.
verses.purport: Tamasic action is reckless, destructive, and blind, disregarding ethical fallout and causing ruin to oneself and society.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
मुक्तसङ्गोऽनहंवादी धृत्युत्साहसमन्वितः |
सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योर्निर्विकारः कर्ता सात्त्विक उच्यते || २६ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
मुक्तसङ्गोऽनहंवादी धृत्युत्साहसमन्वितः |
सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योर्निर्विकारः कर्ता सात्त्विक उच्यते || २६ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
muktasaṅgo'nahaṃvādī dhṛtyutsāhasamanvitaḥ |
siddhyasiddhyornirvikāraḥ kartā sāttvika ucyate || 26 ||
verses.word_meanings: mukta-saṅgaḥ—liberated from attachment; an-ahaṃ-vādī—free from egotism/arrogance; dhṛti-utsāha-samanvitaḥ—endowed with steadfast resolve and enthusiasm; siddhi-asiddhyoḥ—in success or failure; nirvikāraḥ—unaffected / poised; kartā—the doer; sāttvikaḥ ucyate—is called Sattvic.
verses.translation: The worker who is free from attachment, devoid of egotistical pride, endowed with unwavering resolve and enthusiasm, and unperturbed by success or failure—that worker is called Sattvic.
verses.meaning: A Sattvic actor is dynamic yet calm: They combine peak enthusiasm (*Utsaha*) with unshakeable fortitude (*Dhriti*) and complete inner detachment from outcomes.
verses.purport: A Sattvic actor is dynamic yet calm: They combine peak enthusiasm (*Utsaha*) with unshakeable fortitude (*Dhriti*) and complete inner detachment from outcomes.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
रागी कर्मफलप्रेप्सुर्लुब्धो हिंसात्मकोऽशुचिः |
हर्षशोकान्वितः कर्ता राजसः परिकीर्तितः || २७ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
रागी कर्मफलप्रेप्सुर्लुब्धो हिंसात्मकोऽशुचिः |
हर्षशोकान्वितः कर्ता राजसः परिकीर्तितः || २७ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
rāgī karmaphalaprepsurlubdho hiṃsātmako'śuciḥ |
harṣaśokānvitaḥ kartā rājasaḥ parikīrtitaḥ || 27 ||
verses.word_meanings: rāgī—passionate/attached; karma-phala-prepsuḥ—craving the fruits of action; lubdhaḥ—greedy; hiṃsā-ātmakaḥ—cruel/injurious; aśuciḥ—impure; harṣa-śoka-anvitaḥ—subject to elation and despair; kartā—the doer; rājasaḥ—Rajasic; parikīrtitaḥ—is declared.
verses.translation: The worker who is passionate, intensely craving the fruits of action, greedy, harmful to others, impure, and easily swayed by joy and sorrow—that worker is declared to be Rajasic.
verses.meaning: A Rajasic worker is an emotional rollercoaster: Jubilant in victory, devastated in defeat, and willing to compromise ethics out of greed.
verses.purport: A Rajasic worker is an emotional rollercoaster: Jubilant in victory, devastated in defeat, and willing to compromise ethics out of greed.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अयुक्तः प्राकृतः स्तब्धः शठो नैष्कृतिकोऽलसः |
विषादी दीर्घसूत्री च कर्ता तामस उच्यते || २८ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अयुक्तः प्राकृतः स्तब्धः शठो नैष्कृतिकोऽलसः |
विषादी दीर्घसूत्री च कर्ता तामस उच्यते || २८ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
ayuktaḥ prākṛtaḥ stabdhaḥ śaṭho naiṣkṛtiko'lasaḥ |
viṣādī dīrghasūtrī ca kartā tāmasa ucyate || 28 ||
verses.word_meanings: ayuktaḥ—undisciplined; prākṛtaḥ—crude/vulgar; stabdhaḥ—obstinate/arrogant; śaṭhaḥ—deceitful; naiṣkṛtikaḥ—malicious/insulting; alasaḥ—lazy; viṣādī—morose/despondent; dīrgha-sūtrī—procrastinating; ca—and; kartā—doer; tāmasaḥ ucyate—is called Tamasic.
verses.translation: The worker who is undisciplined, vulgar, obstinate, deceitful, malicious, indolent, chronically despondent, and procrastinating—that worker is called Tamasic.
verses.meaning: A Tamasic worker is sluggish, resentful, dishonest, and constantly delaying essential work while sinking into lethargy and depression.
verses.purport: A Tamasic worker is sluggish, resentful, dishonest, and constantly delaying essential work while sinking into lethargy and depression.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
बुद्धेर्भेदं धृतेश्चैव गुणतस्त्रिविधं शृणु |
प्रोच्यमानमशेषेण पृथक्त्वेन धनञ्जय || २९ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
बुद्धेर्भेदं धृतेश्चैव गुणतस्त्रिविधं शृणु |
प्रोच्यमानमशेषेण पृथक्त्वेन धनञ्जय || २९ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
buddherbhedaṃ dhṛteścaiva guṇatastrividhaṃ śṛṇu |
procyamānamaśeṣeṇa pṛthaktvena dhanañjaya || 29 ||
verses.word_meanings: buddheḥ bhedam—the distinction of intellect (Buddhi); dhṛteḥ ca eva—and of determination/fortitude (Dhriti); guṇataḥ—according to the gunas; tri-vidham—threefold; śṛṇu—hear; procyamānam—being explained; aśeṣeṇa—fully/exhaustively; pṛthaktvena—distinctly; dhanañjaya—O Dhananjaya (Arjuna).
verses.translation: Hear now, O Dhananjaya, the threefold distinction of intellect (Buddhi) and fortitude (Dhṛti) according to the Guṇas, explained fully and distinctly by Me.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna expands His psychological map to examine human discernment (Buddhi) and mental willpower (Dhriti).
verses.purport: Sri Krishna expands His psychological map to examine human discernment (Buddhi) and mental willpower (Dhriti).

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
प्रवृत्तिं च निवृत्तिं च कार्याकार्ये भयाभये |
बन्धं मोक्षं च या वेत्ति बुद्धिः सा पार्थ सात्त्विकी || ३० ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
प्रवृत्तिं च निवृत्तिं च कार्याकार्ये भयाभये |
बन्धं मोक्षं च या वेत्ति बुद्धिः सा पार्थ सात्त्विकी || ३० ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
pravṛttiṃ ca nivṛttiṃ ca kāryākārye bhayābhaye |
bandhaṃ mokṣaṃ ca yā vetti buddhiḥ sā pārtha sāttvikī || 30 ||
verses.word_meanings: pravṛttim ca—the path of engagement/action; nivṛttim ca—and the path of renunciation/contemplation; kārya-akārye—what ought to be done and what ought not to be done; bhaya-abhaye—what is fear-inducing and what gives fearlessness; bandham—bondage; mokṣam ca—and liberation; yā vetti—which discerns; buddhiḥ sā—that intellect; pārtha—O Partha; sāttvikī—is Sattvic.
verses.translation: That intellect which understands the paths of engagement and renunciation, what ought to be done and avoided, fear and fearlessness, and bondage and liberation, O Partha, is Sattvic.
verses.meaning: Sattvic Buddhi is clear moral and spiritual vision: It accurately evaluates ethical duties, psychological states, and the path to ultimate liberation.
verses.purport: Sattvic Buddhi is clear moral and spiritual vision: It accurately evaluates ethical duties, psychological states, and the path to ultimate liberation.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यया धर्ममधर्मं च कार्यं चाकार्यमेव च |
अयथावत्प्रजानाति बुद्धिः सा पार्थ राजसी || ३१ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यया धर्ममधर्मं च कार्यं चाकार्यमेव च |
अयथावत्प्रजानाति बुद्धिः सा पार्थ राजसी || ३१ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
yayā dharmamadharmaṃ ca kāryaṃ cākāryameva ca |
ayathāvatprajānāti buddhiḥ sā pārtha rājasī || 31 ||
verses.word_meanings: yayā—by which; dharmam adharmam ca—righteousness and unrighteousness; kāryam ca akāryam eva ca—what ought to be done and what ought not to be done; ayathāvat—imperfectly / in confusion; prajānāti—understands; buddhiḥ sā—that intellect; pārtha—O Partha; rājasī—is Rajasic.
verses.translation: That intellect by which one understands in an imperfect, confused manner what is Dharma and Adharma, and what ought to be done and not done, O Partha, is Rajasic.
verses.meaning: Rajasic intellect is blurred by personal prejudices and self-interest, causing ambiguity and rationalization of wrong actions.
verses.purport: Rajasic intellect is blurred by personal prejudices and self-interest, causing ambiguity and rationalization of wrong actions.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अधर्मं धर्ममिति या मन्यते तमसावृता |
सर्वार्थान्विपरीतांश्च बुद्धिः सा पार्थ तामसी || ३२ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अधर्मं धर्ममिति या मन्यते तमसावृता |
सर्वार्थान्विपरीतांश्च बुद्धिः सा पार्थ तामसी || ३२ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
adharmaṃ dharmamiti yā manyate tamasāvṛtā |
sarvārthānviparītāṃśca buddhiḥ sā pārtha tāmasī || 32 ||
verses.word_meanings: adharmam—unrighteousness; dharmam iti—as righteousness; yā—which; manyate—regards/believes; tamasā-āvṛtā—enshrouded in darkness (Tamas); sarva-arthān—all things; viparītān ca—and inverted/perverted; buddhiḥ sā—that intellect; pārtha—O Partha; tāmasī—is Tamasic.
verses.translation: That intellect which, enshrouded in darkness, looks upon Adharma as Dharma and perceives all things in a perverted and inverted way, O Partha, is Tamasic.
verses.meaning: Tamasic intellect is total inversion: Calling evil good, truth falsehood, and delusion wisdom.
verses.purport: Tamasic intellect is total inversion: Calling evil good, truth falsehood, and delusion wisdom.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
धृत्या यया धारयते मनःप्राणेन्द्रियक्रियाः |
योगेनाव्यभिचारिण्या धृतिः सा पार्थ सात्त्विकी || ३३ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
धृत्या यया धारयते मनःप्राणेन्द्रियक्रियाः |
योगेनाव्यभिचारिण्या धृतिः सा पार्थ सात्त्विकी || ३३ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
dhṛtyā yayā dhārayate manaḥprāṇendriyakriyāḥ |
yogenāvyabhicāriṇyā dhṛtiḥ sā pārtha sāttvikī || 33 ||
verses.word_meanings: dhṛtyā—by determination/fortitude; yayā—by which; dhārayate—controls/sustains; manaḥ-prāṇa-indriya-kriyāḥ—the functions of the mind, vital breath (Prana), and senses; yogena—through yoga/meditation; avyabhicāriṇyā—unswerving/unfaltering; dhṛtiḥ sā—that determination; pārtha—O Partha; sāttvikī—is Sattvic.
verses.translation: That unfaltering determination by which, through the practice of Yoga, one holds and controls the activities of the mind, vital energy (Prāṇa), and senses, O Partha, is Sattvic fortitude.
verses.meaning: Sattvic Dhriti is diamond-hard spiritual willpower that masters the mind and senses and keeps consciousness anchored in God.
verses.purport: Sattvic Dhriti is diamond-hard spiritual willpower that masters the mind and senses and keeps consciousness anchored in God.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यया तु धर्मकामार्थान्धृत्या धारयतेऽर्जुन |
प्रसङ्गेन फलाकाङ्क्षी धृतिः सा पार्थ राजसी || ३४ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यया तु धर्मकामार्थान्धृत्या धारयतेऽर्जुन |
प्रसङ्गेन फलाकाङ्क्षी धृतिः सा पार्थ राजसी || ३४ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
yayā tu dharmakāmārthāndhṛtyā dhārayate'rjuna |
prasaṅgena phalākāṅkṣī dhṛtiḥ sā pārtha rājasī || 34 ||
verses.word_meanings: yayā tu—by which however; dharma-kāma-arthān—duty, pleasure, and wealth; dhṛtyā—by determination; dhārayate—clings to; arjuna—O Arjuna; prasaṅgena—with intense attachment; phala-ākāṅkṣī—desiring fruits; dhṛtiḥ sā—that fortitude; pārtha—O Partha; rājasī—is Rajasic.
verses.translation: But that determination by which one clings obstinately to duty, pleasure, and wealth (Dharma, Kāma, Artha) out of intense attachment and desire for rewards, O Partha, is Rajasic fortitude.
verses.meaning: Rajasic willpower is relentless ambition: Driving hard for wealth, status, and sensual pleasure while calculating profit in every move.
verses.purport: Rajasic willpower is relentless ambition: Driving hard for wealth, status, and sensual pleasure while calculating profit in every move.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यया स्वप्नं भयं शोकं विषादं मदमेव च |
न विमुञ्चति दुर्मेधा धृतिः सा पार्थ तामसी || ३५ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यया स्वप्नं भयं शोकं विषादं मदमेव च |
न विमुञ्चति दुर्मेधा धृतिः सा पार्थ तामसी || ३५ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
yayā svapnaṃ bhayaṃ śokaṃ viṣādaṃ madameva ca |
na vimuñcati durmedhā dhṛtiḥ sā pārtha tāmasī || 35 ||
verses.word_meanings: yayā—by which; svapnam—excessive sleep/laziness; bhayam—fear; śokam—grief; viṣādam—chronic depression; madam eva ca—and arrogance/intoxication; na vimuñcati—does not abandon; durmedhāḥ—the foolish person; dhṛtiḥ sā—that fortitude; pārtha—O Partha; tāmasī—is Tamasic.
verses.translation: That determination by which a foolish person obstinately refuses to give up excessive sleep, fear, grief, chronic depression, and arrogance, O Partha, is Tamasic fortitude.
verses.meaning: Tamasic willpower is stubborn negativity: Holding on firmly to self-pity, resentment, lethargy, and toxic habits.
verses.purport: Tamasic willpower is stubborn negativity: Holding on firmly to self-pity, resentment, lethargy, and toxic habits.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
सुखं त्विदानीं त्रिविधं शृणु मे भरतर्षभ |
अभ्यासाद्रमते यत्र दुःखान्तं च निगच्छति || ३६ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
सुखं त्विदानीं त्रिविधं शृणु मे भरतर्षभ |
अभ्यासाद्रमते यत्र दुःखान्तं च निगच्छति || ३६ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
sukhaṃ tvidānīṃ trividhaṃ śṛṇu me bharatarṣabha |
abhyāsādramate yatra duḥkhāntaṃ ca nigacchati || 36 ||
verses.word_meanings: sukham tu—and happiness; idānīm—now; tri-vidham—threefold; śṛṇu me—hear from Me; bharata-ṛṣabha—O best of the Bharatas; abhyāsāt—through prolonged practice; ramate—one rejoices; yatra—wherein; duḥkha-antam ca—and the end of all suffering; nigacchati—one attains.
verses.translation: Hear now from Me, O best of the Bharatas, of the three kinds of happiness, in which one rejoices through prolonged spiritual practice and comes to the end of all suffering.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna now analyzes the nature of human happiness across the three gunas, leading to supreme transcendence.
verses.purport: Sri Krishna now analyzes the nature of human happiness across the three gunas, leading to supreme transcendence.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यत्तदग्रे विषमिव परिणामेऽमृतोपमम् |
तत्सुखं सात्त्विकं प्रोक्तमात्मबुद्धिप्रसादजम् || ३७ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यत्तदग्रे विषमिव परिणामेऽमृतोपमम् |
तत्सुखं सात्त्विकं प्रोक्तमात्मबुद्धिप्रसादजम् || ३७ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
yattadagre viṣamiva pariṇāme'mṛtopamam |
tatsukhaṃ sāttvikaṃ proktamātmabuddhiprasādajam || 37 ||
verses.word_meanings: yat tat—that which; agre—at the beginning; viṣam iva—like poison; pariṇāme—in the end / outcome; amṛta-upamam—like immortal nectar; tat sukham—that happiness; sāttvikam proktam—is declared to be Sattvic; ātma-buddhi-prasāda-jam—born of the serenity of self-realization.
verses.translation: That happiness which is like poison in the beginning but like immortal nectar in the end, born of the serene clarity of self-realization—that is declared to be Sattvic happiness.
verses.meaning: Sattvic joy requires initial self-discipline (meditation, sensory restraint, study), which feels demanding at first but culminates in everlasting spiritual bliss.
verses.purport: Sattvic joy requires initial self-discipline (meditation, sensory restraint, study), which feels demanding at first but culminates in everlasting spiritual bliss.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
विषयेन्द्रियसंयोगाद्यत्तदग्रेऽमृतोपमम् |
परिणामे विषमिव तत्सुखं राजसं स्मृतम् || ३८ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
विषयेन्द्रियसंयोगाद्यत्तदग्रेऽमृतोपमम् |
परिणामे विषमिव तत्सुखं राजसं स्मृतम् || ३८ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
viṣayendriyasaṃyogādyattadagre'mṛtopamam |
pariṇāme viṣamiva tatsukhaṃ rājasaṃ smṛtam || 38 ||
verses.word_meanings: viṣaya-indriya-saṃyogāt—from the contact of the senses with their objects; yat tat—that which; agre—in the beginning; amṛta-upamam—like nectar; pariṇāme—in the end; viṣam iva—like poison; tat sukham—that pleasure; rājasam smṛtam—is regarded as Rajasic.
verses.translation: That pleasure which arises from the contact of the senses with their objects, which is like nectar in the beginning but like poison in the end—that is regarded as Rajasic pleasure.
verses.meaning: Sensual indulgence thrills the senses immediately, but inevitably turns into satiety, addiction, disease, remorse, and disillusionment.
verses.purport: Sensual indulgence thrills the senses immediately, but inevitably turns into satiety, addiction, disease, remorse, and disillusionment.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यदग्रे चानुबन्धे च सुखं मोहनमात्मनः |
निद्रालस्यप्रमादोत्थं तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् || ३९ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यदग्रे चानुबन्धे च सुखं मोहनमात्मनः |
निद्रालस्यप्रमादोत्थं तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् || ३९ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
yadagre cānubandhe ca sukhaṃ mohanamātmanaḥ |
nidrālasyapramādotthaṃ tattāmasamudāhṛtam || 39 ||
verses.word_meanings: yat—which; agre—at the beginning; ca—and; anubandhe ca—and in the end; sukham—pleasure; mohanam ātmanaḥ—deluding to the soul; nidrā-ālasya-pramāda-uttham—arising from sleep, laziness, and intoxication/heedlessness; tat—that; tāmasam—Tamasic; udāhṛtam—is exemplified.
verses.translation: That pseudo-pleasure which is delusive to the soul from beginning to end, arising from excessive sleep, indolence, and heedlessness—that is declared to be Tamasic.
verses.meaning: Tamasic pleasure is escapism (sleeping all day, substance abuse, vegetative laziness) that destroys consciousness.
verses.purport: Tamasic pleasure is escapism (sleeping all day, substance abuse, vegetative laziness) that destroys consciousness.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
न तदस्ति पृथिव्यां वा दिवि देवेषु वा पुनः |
सत्त्वं प्रकृतिजैर्मुक्तं यदेभिः स्यात्त्रिभिर्गुणैः || ४० ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
न तदस्ति पृथिव्यां वा दिवि देवेषु वा पुनः |
सत्त्वं प्रकृतिजैर्मुक्तं यदेभिः स्यात्त्रिभिर्गुणैः || ४० ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
na tadasti pṛthivyāṃ vā divi deveṣu vā punaḥ |
sattvaṃ prakṛtijairmuktaṃ yadebhiḥ syāttribhirguṇaiḥ || 40 ||
verses.word_meanings: na tat asti—there is no such entity; pṛthivyām vā—either on earth; divi—in heaven; deveṣu vā punaḥ—or even among the demigods; sattvam—being/existence; prakṛti-jaiḥ—born of Prakriti (material nature); muktam—free from; yat—which; ebhiḥ syāt—could be; tribhiḥ guṇaiḥ—these three gunas.
verses.translation: There is no being on earth, nor in heaven among the celestial Devas, that is free from these three Guṇas born of material nature (Prakṛti).
verses.meaning: All embodied life within the cosmic system is subject to the play of the three gunas. Only transcendence through divine surrender liberates.
verses.purport: All embodied life within the cosmic system is subject to the play of the three gunas. Only transcendence through divine surrender liberates.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
ब्राह्मणक्षत्रियविशां शूद्राणां च परन्तप |
कर्माणि प्रविभक्तानि स्वभावप्रभवैर्गुणैः || ४१ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
ब्राह्मणक्षत्रियविशां शूद्राणां च परन्तप |
कर्माणि प्रविभक्तानि स्वभावप्रभवैर्गुणैः || ४१ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
brāhmaṇakṣatriyaviśāṃ śūdrāṇāṃ ca parantapa |
karmāṇi pravibhaktāni svabhāvaprabhavairguṇaiḥ || 41 ||
verses.word_meanings: brāhmaṇa-kṣatriya-viśām—of the intellectual/spiritual, administrative/warrior, and commercial classes; śūdrāṇām ca—and of the artisan/service class; parantapa—O scorcher of foes; karmāṇi—duties/activities; pravibhaktāni—are distributed; svabhāva-prabhavaiḥ guṇaiḥ—by the qualities born of their innate psychological nature (Svabhava).
verses.translation: The duties of the Brāhmaṇas, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, and Śūdras, O scorcher of foes, are categorized according to the qualities born of their innate psychological nature (Svabhāva).
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna explains that vocational duties (Varna) in Vedic society are grounded in psychological qualities and temperaments (Guna and Karma), not mere hereditary birth.
verses.purport: Sri Krishna explains that vocational duties (Varna) in Vedic society are grounded in psychological qualities and temperaments (Guna and Karma), not mere hereditary birth.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
शमो दमस्तपः शौचं क्षान्तिरार्जवमेव च |
ज्ञानं विज्ञानमास्तिक्यं ब्रह्मकर्म स्वभावजम् || ४२ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
शमो दमस्तपः शौचं क्षान्तिरार्जवमेव च |
ज्ञानं विज्ञानमास्तिक्यं ब्रह्मकर्म स्वभावजम् || ४२ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
śamo damastapaḥ śaucaṃ kṣāntirārjavameva ca |
jñānaṃ vijñānamāstikyaṃ brahmakarma svabhāvajam || 42 ||
verses.word_meanings: śamaḥ—tranquility/mind control; damaḥ—sensory restraint; tapaḥ—austerity; śaucam—purity; kṣāntiḥ—forgiveness; ārjavam eva ca—and straightforwardness; jñānam—scriptural knowledge; vijñānam—realized wisdom; āstikyam—faith in Divine Truth; brahma-karma—the duty of a Brahmana; svabhāva-jam—born of one's innate nature.
verses.translation: Tranquility, sense-restraint, austerity, purity, forgiveness, straightforwardness, scriptural knowledge, direct realized wisdom, and firm faith in the Divine Truth—these are the duties of a Brāhmaṇa born of their nature.
verses.meaning: The Brahmana nature is dedicated to contemplation, ethics, teaching, self-mastery, and spiritual realization.
verses.purport: The Brahmana nature is dedicated to contemplation, ethics, teaching, self-mastery, and spiritual realization.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
शौर्यं तेजो धृतिर्दाक्ष्यं युद्ध्यपि चाप्यपलायनम् |
दानमीश्वरभावश्च क्षात्रं कर्म स्वभावजम् || ४३ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
शौर्यं तेजो धृतिर्दाक्ष्यं युद्ध्यपि चाप्यपलायनम् |
दानमीश्वरभावश्च क्षात्रं कर्म स्वभावजम् || ४३ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
śauryaṃ tejo dhṛtidākṣyaṃ yuddhe cāpyapalāyanam |
dānamīśvarabhāvaśca kṣātraṃ karma svabhāvajam || 43 ||
verses.word_meanings: śauryam—heroism/valor; tejaḥ—radiance/majesty; dhṛtiḥ—fortitude/courage; dākṣyam—resourcefulness/skill; yuddhe ca api—and in battle; apalāyanam—not fleeing / standing ground; dānam—magnanimity/generosity; īśvara-bhāvaḥ ca—and leadership/governance; kṣātram karma—the duty of a Kshatriya; svabhāva-jam—born of one's nature.
verses.translation: Heroism, majesty, fortitude, resourcefulness, never fleeing from righteous battle, generosity, and natural leadership—these are the duties of a Kṣatriya born of their nature.
verses.meaning: The Kshatriya nature is noble governance, protection of the weak, courageous defense of Dharma, and righteous administration.
verses.purport: The Kshatriya nature is noble governance, protection of the weak, courageous defense of Dharma, and righteous administration.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
कृषिगौरक्ष्यवाणिज्यं वैश्यकर्म स्वभावजम् |
परिचर्यात्मकं कर्म शूद्रस्यापि स्वभावजम् || ४४ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
कृषिगौरक्ष्यवाणिज्यं वैश्यकर्म स्वभावजम् |
परिचर्यात्मकं कर्म शूद्रस्यापि स्वभावजम् || ४४ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
kṛṣigaurakṣyavāṇijyaṃ vaiśyakarma svabhāvajam |
paricaryātmakaṃ karma śūdrasyāpi svabhāvajam || 44 ||
verses.word_meanings: kṛṣi-gaurakṣya-vāṇijyam—agriculture, cattle protection, and commerce/trade; vaiśya-karma—the duty of a Vaishya; svabhāva-jam—born of nature; paricaryā-ātmakam karma—service, manual craft, and support work; śūdrasya api—of a Shudra as well; svabhāva-jam—born of nature.
verses.translation: Agriculture, cattle rearing, and trade/commerce are the duties of a Vaiśya born of their nature; work consisting of service, labor, and craftsmanship is the duty of a Śūdra born of their nature.
verses.meaning: The economic foundations of society: Wealth generation, agrarian abundance, and supportive craftsmanship, all vital components of the social organism.
verses.purport: The economic foundations of society: Wealth generation, agrarian abundance, and supportive craftsmanship, all vital components of the social organism.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
स्वे स्वे कर्मण्यभिरतः संसिद्धिं लभते नरः |
स्वकर्मनिरतः सिद्धिं यथा विन्दति तच्छृणु || ४५ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
स्वे स्वे कर्मण्यभिरतः संसिद्धिं लभते नरः |
स्वकर्मनिरतः सिद्धिं यथा विन्दति तच्छृणु || ४५ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
sve sve karmaṇyabhirataḥ saṃsiddhiṃ labhate naraḥ |
svakarmanirataḥ siddhiṃ yathā vindati tacchṛṇu || 45 ||
verses.word_meanings: sve sve karmaṇi—each in one's own natural duty; abhirataḥ—devotedly engaged; saṃsiddhim—supreme spiritual perfection; labhate—attains; naraḥ—a person; sva-karma-nirataḥ—one dedicated to one's own duty; siddhim—perfection; yathā—how; vindati—attains; tat śṛṇu—hear that.
verses.translation: Each human being, devotedly engaged in their own natural duty, attains the highest spiritual perfection. Hear now how one dedicated to one's own duty attains this perfection.
verses.meaning: Spiritual liberation is not the exclusive privilege of hermits or monks. Anyone fulfilling their honest calling with devotion attains supreme self-realization.
verses.purport: Spiritual liberation is not the exclusive privilege of hermits or monks. Anyone fulfilling their honest calling with devotion attains supreme self-realization.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यतः प्रवृत्तिर्भूतानां येन सर्वमिदं ततम् |
स्वकर्मणा तमभ्यर्च्य सिद्धिं विन्दति मानवः || ४६ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यतः प्रवृत्तिर्भूतानां येन सर्वमिदं ततम् |
स्वकर्मणा तमभ्यर्च्य सिद्धिं विन्दति मानवः || ४६ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
yataḥ pravṛttirbhūtānāṃ yena sarvamidaṃ tatam |
svakarmaṇā tamabhyarcya siddhiṃ vindati mānavaḥ || 46 ||
verses.word_meanings: yataḥ—from whom; pravṛttiḥ bhūtānām—the emanation and activity of all beings; yena—by whom; sarvam idam—all this creation; tatam—is pervaded; sva-karmaṇā—through one's own work/duty; tam—Him; abhyarcya—worshipping; siddhim vindati—attains perfection; mānavaḥ—a human being.
verses.translation: By worshipping through the dedicated performance of one's own duty Him from whom all beings originate and by whom all this universe is pervaded, a human being attains supreme perfection.
verses.meaning: Work is worship: When daily duty is performed as a direct offering to the All-Pervading Supreme Lord, secular activity transforms into sublime yoga.
verses.purport: Work is worship: When daily duty is performed as a direct offering to the All-Pervading Supreme Lord, secular activity transforms into sublime yoga.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् |
स्वभावनियतं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम् || ४७ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् |
स्वभावनियतं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम् || ४७ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
śreyānsvadharmo viguṇaḥ paradharmātsvanuṣṭhitāt |
svabhāvaniyataṃ karma kurvannāpnoti kilbiṣam || 47 ||
verses.word_meanings: śreyān—far better; sva-dharmaḥ—one's own natural duty; viguṇaḥ—even though devoid of external brilliance / imperfectly performed; para-dharmāt—than another's duty; su-anuṣṭhitāt—well-executed; svabhāva-niyatam karma—duty prescribed by one's innate nature; kurvan—performing; na āpnoti—one does not incur; kilbiṣam—sin / karmic fault.
verses.translation: Far better is one's own natural duty, even though imperfectly executed, than the duty of another well-performed. By performing the work prescribed by one's own nature (Svabhāva), one incurs no sin.
verses.meaning: A cornerstone principle of the Gita: Authenticity to one's own soul-calling (Svadharma) brings inner alignment and liberation. Imitating another's role causes spiritual friction and distress.
verses.purport: A cornerstone principle of the Gita: Authenticity to one's own soul-calling (Svadharma) brings inner alignment and liberation. Imitating another's role causes spiritual friction and distress.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
सहजं कर्म कौन्तेय सदोषमपि न त्यजेत् |
सर्वारम्भा हि दोषेण धूमेनाग्निरिवावृताः || ४८ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
सहजं कर्म कौन्तेय सदोषमपि न त्यजेत् |
सर्वारम्भा हि दोषेण धूमेनाग्निरिवावृताः || ४८ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
sahajaṃ karma kaunteya sadoṣamapi na tyajet |
sarvārambhā hi doṣeṇa dhūmenāgnirivāvṛtāḥ || 48 ||
verses.word_meanings: sahajam karma—the inborn duty; kaunteya—O son of Kunti; sa-doṣam api—even though attended with flaws; na tyajet—one should not abandon; sarva-ārambhāḥ hi—for all undertakings; doṣeṇa—by imperfections/flaws; dhūmena agniḥ iva—as fire is covered by smoke; āvṛtāḥ—are enveloped.
verses.translation: One should not abandon the duty born of one's nature, O Kaunteya, even if it contains flaws. For all undertakings are enveloped by imperfections, just as fire is enveloped by smoke.
verses.meaning: Every human activity in the material realm carries inherent imperfections. Running away into false asceticism will not remove flaws; performing duty with selfless detachment does.
verses.purport: Every human activity in the material realm carries inherent imperfections. Running away into false asceticism will not remove flaws; performing duty with selfless detachment does.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
असक्तबुद्धिः सर्वत्र जितात्मा विगतस्पृहः |
नैष्कर्म्यसिद्धिं परमां संन्यासेनाधिगच्छति || ४९ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
असक्तबुद्धिः सर्वत्र जितात्मा विगतस्पृहः |
नैष्कर्म्यसिद्धिं परमां संन्यासेनाधिगच्छति || ४९ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
asaktabuddhiḥ sarvatra jitātmā vigataspṛhaḥ |
naiṣkarmyasiddhiṃ paramāṃ sannyāsenādhigacchati || 49 ||
verses.word_meanings: asakta-buddhiḥ—one whose intellect is unattached; sarvatra—everywhere; jita-ātmā—whose mind is mastered; vigata-spṛhaḥ—free from craving/desire; naiṣkarmya-siddhim—the perfection of actionlessness (freedom from karma); paramām—supreme; sannyāsena—through true renunciation; adhigacchati—attains.
verses.translation: One whose intellect is unattached everywhere, whose mind is self-mastered, and who is free from all cravings, attains through renunciation the supreme perfection of actionlessness (Naiṣkarmya-siddhi).
verses.meaning: Naiṣkarmya-siddhi is the pinnacle of spiritual freedom: Being fully active in the world while consciousness rests in untouched transcendental stillness.
verses.purport: Naiṣkarmya-siddhi is the pinnacle of spiritual freedom: Being fully active in the world while consciousness rests in untouched transcendental stillness.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
सिद्धिं प्राप्तो यथा ब्रह्म तथाप्नोति निबोध मे |
समासेनैव कौन्तेय निष्ठा ज्ञानस्य या परा || ५० ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
सिद्धिं प्राप्तो यथा ब्रह्म तथाप्नोति निबोध मे |
समासेनैव कौन्तेय निष्ठा ज्ञानस्य या परा || ५० ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
siddhiṃ prāpto yathā brahma tathāpnoti nibodha me |
samāsenaiva kaunteya niṣṭhā jñānasya yā parā || 50 ||
verses.word_meanings: siddhim prāptaḥ—having attained perfection; yathā—how; brahma—Supreme Brahman; tathā—in that manner; āpnoti—attains; nibodha me—learn from Me; samāsena eva—in brief summary; kaunteya—O Kaunteya; niṣṭhā—the state; jñānasya—of knowledge; yā parā—which is supreme.
verses.translation: Learn from Me in brief, O Kaunteya, how one who has attained this perfection reaches Brahman, the supreme state of wisdom.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna now delineates the direct stage-by-stage methodology for realizing the Supreme Brahman (Brahmabhuya).
verses.purport: Sri Krishna now delineates the direct stage-by-stage methodology for realizing the Supreme Brahman (Brahmabhuya).

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
बुद्ध्या विशुद्धया युक्तो धृत्यात्मानं नियम्य च |
शब्दादीन्विषयांस्त्यक्त्वा रागद्वेषौ व्युदस्य च || ५१ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
बुद्ध्या विशुद्धया युक्तो धृत्यात्मानं नियम्य च |
शब्दादीन्विषयांस्त्यक्त्वा रागद्वेषौ व्युदस्य च || ५१ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
buddhyā viśuddhayā yukto dhṛtyātmānaṃ niyamya ca |
śabdādīnviṣayāṃstyaktvā rāgadveṣau vyudasya ca || 51 ||
verses.word_meanings: buddhyā viśuddhayā—with purified intellect; yuktaḥ—endowed; dhṛtyā—with firm fortitude; ātmānam niyamya ca—and restraining the self/mind; śabda-ādīn viṣayān—sound and other sense objects; tyaktvā—relinquishing; rāga-dveṣau—attraction and aversion; vyudasya ca—and casting aside.
verses.translation: Endowed with a purified intellect, restraining the mind with steadfast resolve, turning away from sensory objects such as sound, and casting aside attraction and aversion;
verses.meaning: The contemplative disciplines: Clearing the intellect of mental noise, withdrawing attention from sense turbulence, and freeing the heart from liking and disliking.
verses.purport: The contemplative disciplines: Clearing the intellect of mental noise, withdrawing attention from sense turbulence, and freeing the heart from liking and disliking.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
विविक्तसेवी लघ्वाशी यतवाक्कायमानसः |
ध्यानयोगपरो नित्यं वैराग्यं समुपाश्रितः || ५२ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
विविक्तसेवी लघ्वाशी यतवाक्कायमानसः |
ध्यानयोगपरो नित्यं वैराग्यं समुपाश्रितः || ५२ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
viviktasevī laghvāśī yatavākkāyamānasaḥ |
dhyānayogaparo nityaṃ vairāgyaṃ samupāśritaḥ || 52 ||
verses.word_meanings: vivikta-sevī—dwelling in quiet solitude; laghu-āśī—eating lightly and moderately; yata-vāk-kāya-mānasaḥ—controlling speech, body, and mind; dhyāna-yoga-paraḥ nityam—constantly absorbed in the yoga of meditation; vairāgyam—dispassion; samupāśritaḥ—firmly taking refuge in.
verses.translation: Dwelling in secluded solitude, eating lightly and moderately, with speech, body, and mind thoroughly controlled, constantly absorbed in meditation, and firmly rooted in dispassion;
verses.meaning: The ideal yogic lifestyle: Minimal distraction, light and nourishing diet, silent contemplation, and inner emotional detachment.
verses.purport: The ideal yogic lifestyle: Minimal distraction, light and nourishing diet, silent contemplation, and inner emotional detachment.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अहङ्कारं बलं दर्पं कामं क्रोधं परिग्रहम् |
विमुच्य निर्ममः शान्तो ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते || ५३ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अहङ्कारं बलं दर्पं कामं क्रोधं परिग्रहम् |
विमुच्य निर्ममः शान्तो ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते || ५३ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
ahaṅkāraṃ balaṃ darpaṃ kāmaṃ krodhaṃ parigraham |
vimucya nirmamaḥ śānto brahmabhūyāya kalpate || 53 ||
verses.word_meanings: ahaṅkāram—egotism; balam—arrogant power; darpam—vanity/pride; kāmam—lust/craving; krodham—anger; parigraham—possessiveness/hoarding; vimucya—relinquishing; nirmamaḥ—free from possessiveness ('mine'); śāntaḥ—peaceful; brahma-bhūyāya—for becoming one with Brahman; kalpate—is qualified.
verses.translation: Free from egotism, arrogant force, vanity, lust, anger, and possessiveness, devoid of the sense of 'mine', and ever peaceful—such a seeker is qualified to realize Brahman.
verses.meaning: Shedding the six root obstacles of the ego establishes the seeker in unbroken peace, preparing consciousness for the supreme union with Brahman.
verses.purport: Shedding the six root obstacles of the ego establishes the seeker in unbroken peace, preparing consciousness for the supreme union with Brahman.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
ब्रह्मभूतः प्रसन्नात्मा न शोचति न काङ्क्षति |
समः सर्वेषु भूतेषु मद्भक्तिं लभते पराम् || ५४ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
ब्रह्मभूतः प्रसन्नात्मा न शोचति न काङ्क्षति |
समः सर्वेषु भूतेषु मद्भक्तिं लभते पराम् || ५४ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
brahmabhūtaḥ prasannātmā na śocati na kāṅkṣati |
samaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu madbhaktiṃ labhate parām || 54 ||
verses.word_meanings: brahma-bhūtaḥ—established in Brahman / one with the Supreme Spirit; prasanna-ātmā—serene and joyous in the soul; na śocati—neither grieves; na kāṅkṣati—nor craves; samaḥ—equal/equanimous; sarveṣu bhūteṣu—toward all living beings; mad-bhaktim—supreme devotion to Me; labhate—attains; parām—transcendental/supreme.
verses.translation: Established in Brahman, serene and joyous in the soul, one neither grieves nor craves. Viewing all living beings with universal equanimity, one attains supreme devotion (Parā-Bhakti) unto Me.
verses.meaning: This celebrated verse reveals that non-dual realization of Brahman is not the end of the journey, but the portal into Parā-Bhakti: The highest, purest divine love for Sri Krishna.
verses.purport: This celebrated verse reveals that non-dual realization of Brahman is not the end of the journey, but the portal into Parā-Bhakti: The highest, purest divine love for Sri Krishna.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
भक्त्या मामभिजानाति यावान्यश्चास्मि तत्त्वतः |
ततो मां तत्त्वतो ज्ञात्वा विशते तदनन्तरम् || ५५ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
भक्त्या मामभिजानाति यावान्यश्चास्मि तत्त्वतः |
ततो मां तत्त्वतो ज्ञात्वा विशते तदनन्तरम् || ५५ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
bhaktyā māmabhijānāti yāvānyaścāsmi tattvataḥ |
tato māṃ tattvato jñātvā viśate tadanantaram || 55 ||
verses.word_meanings: bhaktyā—through pure devotion; mām—Me; abhijānāti—one knows in truth; yāvān—how great; yaḥ ca asmi—and what I am; tattvataḥ—in reality; tataḥ—then; mām—Me; tattvataḥ—in truth; jñātvā—having known; viśate—enters into Me / merges in divine communion; tat-anantaram—thereafter.
verses.translation: Through pure devotion one comes to know Me in truth—who I am and what My divine nature is. Then, having known Me in reality, one enters into communion with Me.
verses.meaning: Devotion is the ultimate eye of knowledge: Only love can unlock the complete infinite reality of Bhagavan, culminating in eternal conscious communion.
verses.purport: Devotion is the ultimate eye of knowledge: Only love can unlock the complete infinite reality of Bhagavan, culminating in eternal conscious communion.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
सर्वकर्माण्यपि सदा कुर्वाणो मद्व्यपाश्रयः |
मत्प्रसादादवाप्नोति शाश्वतं पदमव्ययम् || ५६ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
सर्वकर्माण्यपि सदा कुर्वाणो मद्व्यपाश्रयः |
मत्प्रसादादवाप्नोति शाश्वतं पदमव्ययम् || ५६ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
sarvakarmāṇyapi sadā kurvāṇo madvyapāśrayaḥ |
matprasādādavāpnoti śāśvataṃ padamavyayam || 56 ||
verses.word_meanings: sarva-karmāṇi api—even while performing all duties; sadā—always; kurvāṇaḥ—engaged in action; mad-vyapāśrayaḥ—taking complete shelter in Me; mat-prasādāt—by My divine grace; avāpnoti—attains; śāśvatam—the eternal; padam avyayam—imperishable abode.
verses.translation: Even though constantly engaged in all kinds of activities, one who takes complete shelter in Me reaches by My grace the eternal, imperishable supreme abode.
verses.meaning: One does not need to abandon active life in the world: Dedicated surrender to Krishna consecrates every deed and guarantees eternal liberation by divine grace.
verses.purport: One does not need to abandon active life in the world: Dedicated surrender to Krishna consecrates every deed and guarantees eternal liberation by divine grace.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
चेतसा सर्वकर्माणि मयि संन्यस्य मत्परः |
बुद्धियोगमुपाश्रित्य मच्चित्तः सततं भव || ५७ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
चेतसा सर्वकर्माणि मयि संन्यस्य मत्परः |
बुद्धियोगमुपाश्रित्य मच्चित्तः सततं भव || ५७ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
cetasā sarvakarmāṇi mayi sannyasya matparaḥ |
buddhiyogamupāśritya maccittaḥ satataṃ bhava || 57 ||
verses.word_meanings: cetasā—with your mind; sarva-karmāṇi—all actions; mayi—in Me; sannyasya—surrendering; mat-paraḥ—regarding Me as supreme; buddhi-yogam—the yoga of intellect/discernment; upāśritya—taking refuge in; mat-cittaḥ—mind fixed on Me; satatam—constantly; bhava—become.
verses.translation: Mentally dedicating all your actions unto Me, regarding Me as your supreme goal, and taking shelter in the yoga of intellect (Buddhi Yoga), keep your mind constantly focused on Me.
verses.meaning: A direct practical instruction: Consecrate every thought, word, and deed to Krishna, maintaining an unbroken inner dialogue with the Divine.
verses.purport: A direct practical instruction: Consecrate every thought, word, and deed to Krishna, maintaining an unbroken inner dialogue with the Divine.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
मच्चित्तः सर्वदुर्गाणि मत्प्रसादात्तरिष्यसि |
अथ चेत्त्वमहङ्कारान्न श्रोष्यसि विनङ्क्ष्यसि || ५८ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
मच्चित्तः सर्वदुर्गाणि मत्प्रसादात्तरिष्यसि |
अथ चेत्त्वमहङ्कारान्न श्रोष्यसि विनङ्क्ष्यसि || ५८ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
maccittaḥ sarvadurgāṇi matprasādāttariṣyasi |
atha cettvamahaṅkārānna śroṣyasi vinaṅkṣyasi || 58 ||
verses.word_meanings: mat-cittaḥ—with mind fixed on Me; sarva-durgāṇi—all obstacles and perils; mat-prasādāt—by My grace; tariṣyasi—you will cross over; atha cet—if however; tvam—you; ahaṅkārāt—out of egotistical pride; na śroṣyasi—do not listen; vinaṅkṣyasi—you will perish / meet ruin.
verses.translation: Fixing your mind on Me, you shall by My divine grace cross over all obstacles and perils. But if out of egotistical pride you do not listen to Me, you will perish.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna offers absolute protection to the surrendered soul, but warns that obstinate egoism leads directly to spiritual and existential ruin.
verses.purport: Sri Krishna offers absolute protection to the surrendered soul, but warns that obstinate egoism leads directly to spiritual and existential ruin.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यदहङ्कारमाश्रित्य न योत्स्य इति मन्यसे |
मिथ्यैष व्यवसायस्ते प्रकृतिस्त्वां नियोक्ष्यति || ५९ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यदहङ्कारमाश्रित्य न योत्स्य इति मन्यसे |
मिथ्यैष व्यवसायस्ते प्रकृतिस्त्वां नियोक्ष्यति || ५९ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
yadahaṅkāramāśritya na yotsya iti manyase |
mithyaiṣa vyavasāyaste prakṛtistvāṃ niyokṣyati || 59 ||
verses.word_meanings: yat—if; ahaṅkāram āśritya—taking shelter in egotism; na yotsye iti—'I will not fight'; manyase—you think; mithyā eṣaḥ—vain/futile is this; vyavasāyaḥ te—your resolve; prakṛtiḥ—your Kshatriya warrior nature; tvām—you; niyokṣyati—will compel/engage.
verses.translation: If, taking shelter in egotism, you think 'I will not fight', vain is this resolve of yours; for your own Kshatriya nature will compel you.
verses.meaning: Psychological realism: One cannot suppress one's deep-seated constitutional nature (Svabhava) through artificial, sentimentally conceived pacifism.
verses.purport: Psychological realism: One cannot suppress one's deep-seated constitutional nature (Svabhava) through artificial, sentimentally conceived pacifism.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
स्वभावजेन कौन्तेय निबद्धः स्वेन कर्मणा |
कर्तुं नेच्छसि यन्मोहात्करिष्यस्यवशोऽपि तत् || ६० ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
स्वभावजेन कौन्तेय निबद्धः स्वेन कर्मणा |
कर्तुं नेच्छसि यन्मोहात्करिष्यस्यवशोऽपि तत् || ६० ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
svabhāvajena kaunteya nibaddhaḥ svena karmaṇā |
kartuṃ necchasi yanmohāt kariṣyasyavaśo'pi tat || 60 ||
verses.word_meanings: svabhāva-jena—born of your innate nature; kaunteya—O son of Kunti; nibaddhaḥ—bound; svena karmaṇā—by your own karma; kartum na icchasi—what you do not wish to do; yat mohāt—which out of delusion; kariṣyasi—you will do; avaśaḥ api—helplessly / inevitably; tat—that.
verses.translation: Bound by your own karma born of your nature, O Kaunteya, that which out of delusion you now wish not to do, you will perform inevitably and helplessly.
verses.meaning: Inner samskaras and warrior duty cannot be avoided: It is far wiser to fight consciously as a yoga offering to God than to be dragged into it helplessly by circumstance.
verses.purport: Inner samskaras and warrior duty cannot be avoided: It is far wiser to fight consciously as a yoga offering to God than to be dragged into it helplessly by circumstance.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
ईश्वरः सर्वभूतानां हृद्देशेऽर्जुन तिष्ठति |
भ्रामयन्सर्वभूतानि यन्त्रारूढानि मायया || ६१ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
ईश्वरः सर्वभूतानां हृद्देशेऽर्जुन तिष्ठति |
भ्रामयन्सर्वभूतानि यन्त्रारूढानि मायया || ६१ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
īśvaraḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ hṛddeśe'rjuna tiṣṭhati |
bhrāmayansarvabhūtāni yantrārūḍhāni māyayā || 61 ||
verses.word_meanings: īśvaraḥ—the Supreme Lord; sarva-bhūtānām—of all living beings; hṛt-deśe—in the region of the heart; arjuna—O Arjuna; tiṣṭhati—dwells/resides; bhrāmayan—causing to revolve/move; sarva-bhūtāni—all living entities; yantra-ārūḍhāni—mounted on a cosmic machine (the psycho-physical body); māyayā—by the power of His Maya.
verses.translation: The Supreme Lord dwells in the heart of all beings, O Arjuna, causing all beings to revolve by His illusory power (Māyā), as if mounted on a cosmic machine.
verses.meaning: The Lord is not a distant ruler in the skies; He is the Antaryamin (Inner Ruler) seated in every heart, orchestrating the cosmic mechanism of nature according to each soul's karma.
verses.purport: The Lord is not a distant ruler in the skies; He is the Antaryamin (Inner Ruler) seated in every heart, orchestrating the cosmic mechanism of nature according to each soul's karma.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
तमेव शरणं गच्छ सर्वभावेन भारत |
तत्प्रसादात्परां शान्तिं स्थानं प्राप्स्यसि शाश्वतम् || ६२ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
तमेव शरणं गच्छ सर्वभावेन भारत |
तत्प्रसादात्परां शान्तिं स्थानं प्राप्स्यसि शाश्वतम् || ६२ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
tameva śaraṇaṃ gaccha sarvabhāvena bhārata |
tatprasādātparāṃ śāntiṃ sthānaṃ prāpsyasi śāśvatam || 62 ||
verses.word_meanings: tam eva—unto Him alone; śaraṇam gaccha—take complete refuge / surrender; sarva-bhāvena—with your whole being and heart; bhārata—O descendant of Bharata; tat-prasādāt—by His divine grace; parām śāntim—supreme transcendental peace; sthānam—abode; prāpsyasi—you shall attain; śāśvatam—the eternal.
verses.translation: Surrender unto Him alone with all your being, O Bharata. By His divine grace you shall attain supreme transcendental peace and the eternal, imperishable abode.
verses.meaning: Total surrender (*Sharanagati*) to the indwelling Lord is the royal key that unlocks absolute peace and lifts the seeker out of the revolving machine of Maya.
verses.purport: Total surrender (*Sharanagati*) to the indwelling Lord is the royal key that unlocks absolute peace and lifts the seeker out of the revolving machine of Maya.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
इति ते ज्ञानमाख्यातं गुह्याद्गुह्यतरं मया |
विमृश्यैतदशेषेण यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु || ६३ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
इति ते ज्ञानमाख्यातं गुह्याद्गुह्यतरं मया |
विमृश्यैतदशेषेण यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु || ६३ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
iti te jñānamākhyātaṃ guhyādguhyataraṃ mayā |
vimṛśyaitadaśeṣeṇa yathecchasi tathā kuru || 63 ||
verses.word_meanings: iti—thus; te—unto you; jñānam—wisdom/knowledge; ākhyātam—has been expounded; guhyāt guhyataram—more confidential than the most secret; mayā—by Me; vimṛśya—reflecting upon / analyzing; etat—this; aśeṣeṇa—fully / in its entirety; yathā icchasi—as you wish; tathā kuru—do so.
verses.translation: Thus has this wisdom, more confidential than the secret of secrets, been expounded to you by Me. Reflecting upon this in its entirety, act as you choose.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna's supreme respect for human free will: God enlightens and illuminates, but never coerces. Having shared the complete truth, He invites Arjuna to contemplate deeply and make his own conscious decision.
verses.purport: Sri Krishna's supreme respect for human free will: God enlightens and illuminates, but never coerces. Having shared the complete truth, He invites Arjuna to contemplate deeply and make his own conscious decision.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
सर्वगुह्यतमं भूयः शृणु मे परमं वचः |
इष्टोऽसि मे दृढमिति ततो वक्ष्यामि ते हितम् || ६४ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
सर्वगुह्यतमं भूयः शृणु मे परमं वचः |
इष्टोऽसि मे दृढमिति ततो वक्ष्यामि ते हितम् || ६४ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
sarvaguhyatamaṃ bhūyaḥ śṛṇu me paramaṃ vacaḥ |
iṣṭo'si me dṛḍhamiti tato vakṣyāmi te hitam || 64 ||
